INTRODUCTION
This document is the User Guide for Product Usage API within the framework of the GSMA
Open
Gateway
initiative,
enabling
automated
usage
exchange
and
settlement
between
Operators and Channel Partners.
This API is inspired by TMF635 Product Usage API v5.0 for Open Gateway context.
The
GSMA
Open
Gateway
initiative
defines
standardized
Service
APIs
and
Service
Management APIs,
complemented
by
a
common
set
of
Operate APIs
that
provide
cross-
cutting commercial and operational capabilities. These Operate APIs define homogeneous
integration mechanisms between Operators and Channel Partners to ensure interoperability
across networks and markets.
By defining clear and consistent API requirements, this document supports alignment with
industry
best
practices
and
facilitates
communication
among
stakeholders
in
the
Open
Gateway
ecosystem. This
version
focuses
on
the
Usage
Consumption
Reporting
function
within
the
Operate
API
suite,
while
future
versions
may
include
other
Channel
Partner
integration capabilities such as service assurance, monitoring, and settlement automation.
OVERVIEW OF GSMA OPEN GATEWAY AND CHANNEL PARTNER
MODEL
Open
Gateway
is
a
GSMA-led
initiative
in
the
telecommunications
sector
that
turns
communication
networks
into
platforms
by
exposing
telco
capabilities
through
industry-
standard
APIs
on
a
global
scale
under
the
CAMARA
open-source
project.
CAMARA
is
hosted by the Linux Foundation and provides the technical framework for these standardized
APIs.
Channel Partners are key go-to-market players for Operators that want to sell APIs to many
Developers
who
do
not
want
to
integrate
individually
with
each
Operator.
By
aggregating
multiple
Operators’
APIs
into
a
single
Operator-agnostic
interface,
Channel
Partners
can
offer these capabilities to a wide community of application Developers.
Channel Partner model overview
Open Gateway Channel Partner model is composed of different players:
•
End Users are both subscribers to Operators and users of the application published by
the Developers.
•
Developers
(Application
Owner
Organization)
build
and
own
the
applications
that
consume
APIs
from
the
Operators
to
provide
End
Users
with
enhanced
features
or
enable new use cases.
•
Channel
Partners
aggregate
Operators'
CAMARA
standardised
APIs
to
build
Open
Services and implement Operator end-point routing based on final user identification on
the networks.
•
Operators
expose
telco
capabilities
through
CAMARA
standardised
APIs
and
could
partner with Channel Partners to enable the Services that they offer to Developers.

Channel Partner and leverages Open Gateway products such as QoD to enhance mobile
gaming
experiences.
The
ability
of
Operators
and
Channel
Partners
to
form
agreements
directly affects which subscribers can access those enhanced services.
Two gamers using the same game but different mobile Operators are mapped to different
Operator–Channel Partner relationships, as shown in the relational diagram.
Example Interaction between players on the model
Operate APIs
As
indicated,
the
Channel
Partner
indirect
model
enables
a
single
channel
for
tenant
applications to gain access to capabilities from multiple Operators, without the need for the
customer
to
set
up
a
contractual
relationship
with
each
of
them.
It
is
clear
the
need
to
provide certain additional functionalities from the Operators to the Channel Partner to enable
the commercial model.

Page 3
Therefore,
in
addition
to
the
CAMARA APIs,
the
Operate APIs
are
proposed
for
offering
programmable access to Operation, Administration and Management (OAM) capabilities to
facilitate the integration of the Open Gateway NaaS Platform with Channel Partner. These
APIs provide all the transversal/non-service specific functionalities that are required to make
a commercial product out of the Service APIs and Service Management APIs, making them
operable
and
monetizable.
Examples
of
functions
provided
by
the
Operate
APIs
include
ordering,
usage
consumption
reporting,
monitoring,
trouble
ticketing,
accounting,
billing,
payment, etc., but also API discovery, user registration and consent management, etc.
Scope
This specification focuses on the Usage Consumption Reporting function within the Operate
API
suite.
Its
purpose
is
to
define
the
requirements
and
aggregated
file
structure
for
exchanging
ProductUsage
data
between
Operators
and
Channel
Partners. This
capability
enables
automation
of
the
usage
collection,
reporting,
and
settlement
process,
which
is
essential
for
monetizing
Open
Gateway
APIs
in
both
the
Wholesale
Reseller
and
Marketplace Aggregator
models.
Operators
record
each
invocation
of
CAMARA APIs
and
transform those invocations into ProductUsage records, following the TM Forum Open API
and SID information models. These ProductUsage records are then aggregated and shared
in bulk with Channel Partners via the Usage Operate API.
Commercial Models Supported
Model
Description
Wholesale Reseller
The Channel Partner manages the service,
defines its own end-user products and pricing,
and receives usage data from the Operator for
settlement.
Marketplace Aggregator
The Operator defines the product and pricing; the
Channel Partner resells it and requires usage
data that already includes rated information for
end-user billing.
Open Gateway Product Usage User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 4
In
both
models,
the
basis
of
exchange
is
a
structured
set
of
ProductUsage
records
containing sufficient attributes to enable pricing, billing, and reconciliation. These records are
equivalent to CDRs (Call Detail Records) or EDRs (Event Detail Records). The difference
lies in whether pricing details are included (Marketplace) or applied later (Wholesale), i.e.
rated or non-rated.
Key Differentiator – What’s New for Usage
Compared
with
other
Operate
APIs
such
as
Ordering,
the
Product
Usage
Operate
API
introduces several specific capabilities.
•
A standardized ProductUsage data model aligned with TMF635 v5.0 Product Usage API.
•
An embedded ExportJob mechanism for asynchronous bulk data transfer, aligned with
TMF635 evolution.
•
Defined file and metadata structures using ZIP, JSON and signatures for auditability and
interoperability.
•
Support for mutual TLS to ensure trusted exchange between parties.
•
Compatibility with both Marketplace and Wholesale commercial models.
These
differentiators
make
the
Product
Usage
Operate
API
a
bridge
between
the
commercial product catalog and operational monetization layer. Once APIs are defined and
offered in the Operator’s catalog, the Product Usage Operate API provides the mechanism
for exchanging measured usage data that directly relates to those catalog entries and pricing
models.
Catalog Alignment
The Product Usage Operate API complements the TMF936 Open Gateway Product Catalog
API by defining how usage of catalogued CAMARA APIs is measured, recorded, and shared
between the Operator and Channel Partner. In other words, while the catalog defines what is
being offered (e.g., QoD, SIM Swap, Number Verification) and under what commercial terms,
the Product Usage Operate API defines how the consumption of those offers is operationally
reported and monetized. The two together — catalog definition and usage reporting — form
the foundation for automated settlement and revenue assurance across the Open Gateway
ecosystem.
The catalog for Operator-exposed APIs includes:
•
A CAMARA standardized API available on the Operator’s exposure platform.
•
Defined
API
scopes
(e.g.,
check-sim-swap,
verify-number)
and
corresponding
usage
characteristics.
•
Supported charging models (one-shot, recurring, usage-based).
•
Applicable purposes and constraints (privacy, SLA, or policy).
The
Product
Usage
Operate
API
extends
this
catalog
context
by
standardizing
the
ProductUsage exchange for each CAMARA API and aligning usage characteristics with the
corresponding
ProductUsageSpecification
that
can
be
defined
in
TMF767
Product
Usage
Catalog API.

SAMPLE USE CASES
Usage refers to the specific instances of Open Gateway API service consumption by end
users or applications. These events capture critical data about how, when and by whom a
service was used and the products used in the Operator to authorize that service usage.
They are the foundational data that drives billing, revenue sharing, and operational insights.
Its meticulous tracking and transparent reporting are vital to the integrity and efficiency of
modern telecom ecosystems.
In the context of the GSMA Playbook, the Operate API related to Usage are in the context of
exchanging
data
between
the
Operator
and
the
Channel
Partner
but
could
also
be
considered in the context of a direct relationship between Operator and Developer.
The exchange of information between an Operator and a Channel Partner can be done in a
Wholesale Reseller or a Marketplace Aggregator Model:
Wholesale Reseller Model
Marketplace Aggregator Model
Services fully managed by the Channel Partner
Channel Partner enters an agreement with
Operators for their services
Channel Partner manages the end user products,
performs pricing and invoices developer
Operator provides the underlying service and
tracks the usage
Operator provides the Channel Partner with the
usage to support them in billing processes and for
reconciliation.
Operator provides the service at a wholesale rate
and invoices the Channel Partner
Channel Partner deduct a percentage fee to the
amount paid by the Developer and make an
account deposit to the Operator for the remaining
amount
Operators upload their products to the Channel
Partner’s Marketplace and enter an agreement
for their services
Channel Partners provide a unified interface for
developers to ensure a coherent user experience
Developers purchase products from the
Marketplace
Operator provides the underlying service and
tracks the usage
The usage is priced according to the Operator’s
product definition
Operator provides the Channel Partner with the
priced usage required to support them in their
invoicing process
Operator keeps track of their revenue share
based on the priced usage and invoices Channel
Partner
For both models, the basis of the information exchange is sufficient details of the use of the
APIs
to
be
able
to
price
the
event
based
on
required
attributes
according
to
the
product
definition.
The
key
difference
between
the
two
types
is
that
the
Marketplace
Aggregator
Model includes how the Operator charged for the CAMARA API usage events based on the
product definition. The requirements in this chapter focus on the requirements on the usage
consumption exchange between the Operator and Channel Partner for both models above.

#
Summary
Comment
GSMA0
Definition of a unified way to
report usage information of the
Open Gateway services, so that
aggregators/Channel Partners
can make it available to the
developers accordingly.
Information related to
consumption of Service APIs is
managed by the Operators who
are the ones who have an end-
to-end view of the services and
network resources. This
information is exposed towards
aggregators/Channel Partners
for consolidation and billing
management.
GSMA1
Service Charging process will be
performed based on the
consumption of the Open
Gateway Products and will
involve the following: Charging
Calculation: charging calculation
will be implemented by the
Operator based on the
consumption of the specific API
Operations. The calculation will
be performed based on billable
concepts that could be different
depending on the Open
Gateway Product. Examples of
these billable concepts are
contracting, exchange, time
duration, data volume or
characteristics (modifiers). The
information associated to these
billable concepts will be
managed by Operators, as they
have the control of details of the
Open Gateway Product
execution. Operators will
implement the required
calculation process (guiding) to
generate CDRs (Call Detail
Records) or EDRs (Event Detail
Records) which include the
associated data and rating to
calculate price.
In the context of TM Forum, the
CDR/EDR is not an entity but
the CDR/EDR concept
corresponds to the Usage entity.
The exchange of information by
an Operator to an external party
is done on Product Usage level
based on the underlying Service
Usage. The focus for the
Operate API will be to exchange
the Product Usage information
but to do so, there needs to be
an understanding of what
elements of the Service Usage
to bring in and surface as well
as adding Product Usage
attributes, for example pricing
elements.
Open Gateway Product Usage User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 7
#
Summary
Comment
GSMA2
Share usage information from
Operator to Channel Partner to
be able to generate the required
billable information. Operators
are responsible for implementing
the mechanism to share this
information with the Channel
Partners. Charging information
could be shared using two
different approaches.
* Operator exposes information
to Channel Partner: the charging
information will be exposed by
the Operator using Operate
APIs that the Channel Partner
can invoke. Operators should
implement these APIs and make
them available to Channel
Partners that will implement the
associated process to manage
charging information. * Operator
loads the information onto the
Channel Partner: the charging
information will be loaded to the
Channel Partner systems by
invoking their proprietary APIs.
Channel Partners usually
implement these types of APIs
as part of their standard service.
Operators need to implement
the associated process to load
the required charging
information.
In the context of Operate API
Usage definition, the first
approach is applicable.
However, the content of the data
exchanged in both cases should
be similar for the same type of
service. The pull mechanism,
frequency etc. will need to be
considered due to the expected
high volumes of data to be
exchanged.
GSMA3
Billable concepts are defined as
a feature associated with the
Service that can be measured
and accounted for, and to which
a value is assigned. The billing
process will use these values to
charge for the Service.
See the initial list of billable
concepts for more details

Operate APIs * The Operate

and billing flows are for

Product Usage Requirements
Each Open Gateway Service API needs its own definition of Product Usage Specification for
Wholesale and for Marketplace Aggregator model to exchange information for the Channel
Partner
to
be
able
to
use
the
data
for
developer
billing,
revenue
share,
and
settlement
reconciliation (note this is not the settlement in itself, but the data that underpins such an
invoice). The difference in the usage event details provided between the two models is that
the pricing section is not mandatory in the Wholesale model (could be included depending
on the particular agreement between the Operator and the Channel Partner to contain the
wholesale
rate)
but
is
required
for
the
Marketplace Aggregator
model.
In

section

minimum
amount
of

that

allow

Partners

create

and
expose
usage
to
Developers
and
enable

of

usage
between
Channel Partners and Operators. The usage exchange is at Product level between Operator
and
Channel
Partner,
where
the
Product
Usage
is
built
upon
internal
Operator’s
relevant
Service Usage events that are not shared with the Channel Partner. As a general principle,
due to privacy reasons, the information to be exposed doesn’t include any final user data
that could be considered as personal information (for instance MSISDN).

Mechanism for Usage Exchange
There is a need to exchange the Usage data between Operator and Channel Partner in an
efficient
and
timely
way
considering
that
it
is
a
large
volume
of
data.
It
needs
to
support
various use cases such as reporting for an Application Owner, internal analytics for Channel
Partner, dashboards, operational support including complaints, etc. The key requirement is
to provide a mechanism to exchange a bulk of usage data for settlement reconciliation and
billing. In the future, online queries and on-demand reporting may be considered.
Bulk Transfer
TMF937 adopts a bulk export approach, modeled on the TM Forum ExportJob pattern and
aligned with GSMA BCE (Billing and Charging Evolution) practices. This pattern is especially
important in high-volume scenarios like CAMARA API monetization.
Frequency of data exchange
Operators should be able to export usage records on a regular schedule — such as hourly,
daily, or weekly — depending on partner needs and system capabilities. This flexibility allows
the model to support both near-real-time usage and end-of-day settlement workflows. In the
first version it is assumed that the schedule is part of the Agreement and is set up by the
Operator.
In
future
versions
we
may
also
include
the
possibility
to
set
up
on-demand
subscriptions by the Channel Partner.

File Contents
Each exported file includes zero or more ProductUsage records. If no usage event exists for
a reported time period, a file is produced but it contains 0 ProductUsage indicating an empty
file. These records reference a ProductUsageSpecification, defined separately in the catalog
via TMF936 (planned in a future version), so partners understand how to interpret the usage
event characteristics. Records may optionally include pricing details (usageProductPrice) —
required in Marketplace Aggregator models where the Operator handles first level rating.

Date and Time Stamps
To ensure consistency and avoid ambiguity across systems and time zones, all dates and
times
in

(YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ)

(denoted

This

Mutual TLS (Two-Way SSL) Authentication for Report File Consumption
The system shall enforce two-way SSL (mutual TLS) authentication for all HTTPS requests
made to the /exportJob endpoint. This ensures that both the data server and the consuming
Channel Partner authenticate each other before any report files are exchanged and that the
Channel Partner only has access to the data pertaining to their agreement with the Operator.
•
During
onboarding,
each
Channel
Partner
must
register
a
public
certificate
with
the
Operator.
•
When
invoking
/exportJob,
the
partner
must
use
the
corresponding
private
key
to
establish the TLS session.
•
The server must validate the presented certificate against the registered public key.
•
Requests from unrecognized or invalid certificates must be rejected.
•
The validated partner identity must be used as a claim in report generation to guarantee
the file is associated only with the authenticated partner.
•
All report downloads must be served only over authenticated and encrypted connections.
For
transferring
sensitive
files,
HTTPS
and
SFTP
can
both
be
very
secure
if
configured
correctly, but for pure system-to-system file exchange SFTP is usually preferable because it
is purpose built for file operations and naturally encourages strong key-based authentication
and end-to-end encryption. HTTPS can be equally strong cryptographically and is the better
choice when you need browser access or integration with existing web/API security (OAuth,
mTLS, WAFs, etc.).
For now, only SFTP is considered for TMF937 first version.
Download links should always be short-lived and bound to the authenticated API client who
requested them by using JWT time-limited tokens. Additionally, access to the file itself must
require prior authentication so that the link cannot be used without verifying the API client
identity.

Reconciliation between Operator and Channel Partner
For both Wholesale Reseller and Marketplace Aggregator models, sufficient details need to
be provided to be able to reconcile the use of the service reported as Product Usage with the
amount
owed
based
on
the
API
Usage
and
product
definition.
For
Wholesale
Reseller
agreements the Operator invoices the Channel Partner based on the API Usage for a given
period at the agreed wholesale rate. For Aggregated Marketplace agreements, the Channel
Partner provides a statement of the calculation of the revenue share that is to be deposited
to the Operator.

Creation of Product Usage (Pre-requisite)
This use case describes the E2E flow of how usage is created to enable the exposure of the
usage data to the Channel Partner. It is in the context of TMF937 a pre-requisite to explain
the data creation prior to exchanging the data from Operator to Channel Partner.
•
Developer invokes a CAMARA API operation via Channel Partner.
•
Channel Partner forwards request to Operator.
•
Operator invokes the actual service and receives enriched response.
•
Operator forwards the response to the application and sends enriched charging request
internally.
•
Operator charging guides the API to the appropriate product and applies product rules
according to the product catalog definition including the definition of the characteristics of
the event based on the associated Product Usage Specification.
•
A ProductUsage record is created, including:
◦
Party identifiers (Application, Channel Partner)
◦
CorrelationID
◦
API event characteristics
◦
Pricing information (if applicable)

File content
Product Usage
In
the
context
of
TMF937
,
a
ProductUsage
record
represents
the
structured
report
of
a
service that has been delivered, guided to a product and is considered billable. It captures
the
essential
information
needed
for
monetization,
settlement,
and
reconciliation
between an Operator and a Channel Partner.
Each
ProductUsage
record
is
defined
by
a
corresponding
ProductUsageSpecification
,
which standardizes
what type of usage occurred
(e.g., API call, session, data query) and
its
associated
characteristics
(e.g.,
correlation
ID,
duration,
geo
scope).
This
separation
ensures consistent modeling across different offers and CSP implementations.
While
ProductUsage
is
generally
agnostic
of
pricing
logic
,
its
role
depends
on
the
monetization model
:
•
In
a
marketplace
aggregator
model
,
the
operator
performs
the
rating,
and
the
ProductUsage
record
will
include
priced
values
(e.g.,
cost,
tier
applied,
currency)
to
reflect the final charge to the channel partner or developer.
•
In
a
wholesale
model
,
the
ProductUsage
may
be
exchanged
as
a
processed
usage
record
with the relevant characteristics, but with pricing determined by the aggregator.
TMF937
ensures
that
this
usage
data
can
be
exchanged
efficiently,
transparently,
and
interoperably
, supporting:
•
Standardized usage structures across parties
•
Optional inclusion of pricing context when required
•
Accurate and auditable monetization across B2B2X ecosystems
In
TMF937,
ProductUsage
is
not
created
or
modified
by
the
API
—
it
is
exported
.
The
Operator’s
systems
remain
the
system
of
record;
TMF937
defines
only
the
format
and
delivery mechanism
for exchanging usage data with Channel Partners. This model enables
CSPs
to
scale
participation
in
Open
Gateway
by
aligning
technical
API
behavior
with
commercial
execution
,
and
providing
the
data
foundations
for
automated
rating,
invoicing, and dispute resolution
.

Resource
The resource that is the basis of the TMF937 API is ProductUsage as defined in TMF635
v5.0.
TMF937
is
responsible
for
exchanging
the
data
between
the
Operator
and
the
Channel
Partner. How the ProductUsage is created and maintained is internal to the Operator and is
not applicable for TMF937. What usageProperties that is applicable for a given usage event
is determined by the ProductUsageSpecification as part of the ProductOffering.
UsageProductPrice is only required for Marketplace Aggregator model cases where prices
are determined by Operator.

Attribute
Exclusion Rationale

no GET /productUsage operation yet so would
not be valued

no requirement

replaced by usageProperties for strongly typed
characteristics
relatedParty
no requirement
externalIdentifier
no requirement
usageSpecification
no need for MVP as the specification is
materialized in the schema referred via
schemaLocation. May be added in the future if
there are requirements.
serviceUsage
Internal reference to network/service layer usage;
not relevant to Channel Partner.
usageProductPrice.priceAlteration
usageProductPrice.productOfferingPrice
usageProductPrice.recurringChargePeriod
usageProductPrice.unitOfMeasure
usageProductPrice.priceType
usageProductPrice.name
Simplified out of MVP; price per record captured
in UsageProductPrice if applicable. No need for
additional information.
usageProductPrice.price.percentage
usageProductPrice.price.taxIncludedAmount
usageProductPrice.price.taxRate
Not relevant in B2B2X exchange; all pricing duty-
free and tax applied at later billing stages.
Future versions may consider reintroducing some of these attributes as optional, depending
on Open Gateway marketplace models.

Structure and Relationship
Each
ProductUsage
record
references
a
ProductUsageSpecification
that
defines
the
expected
characteristics,
such
as
usage
type,
reporting
dimensions,
and
correlation
keys.
TMF937 packages multiple ProductUsage records into a bulk exchange file, accompanied
by metadata describing the batch context (period, count, and serving/served parties).
ProductUsage 1..* ¬ definedBy ¬ ProductUsageSpecification 1
ProductUsage 1..1 ¬ exportedThrough ¬ ExportJob 1
Lifecycle and Exchange Status Policy
This section defines the valid
status values
for ProductUsage and clarifies
which states
are
eligible
for
exchange
between
the
Operator
(Serving
Party)
and
Channel
Partner
(Served
Party).
The
intent
is
to
ensure
that
only
finalized
and
commercially
meaningful
usage data is shared, while intermediate or error states remain internal to the Operator.
The
standard
ProductUsage
lifecycle
is
defined
in
TMF635,
including
operational
and
validation states.
The
Product
Usage
that
is
to
be
shared
between
the
Operator
and
the
Channel
Partner
should be as follows:
Model
Description
Shared Status
Marketplace
Aggregator Model
Operator performs rating before exchange;
shared usage includes monetary values.
rated
Wholesale Model
Operator shares validated, unrated usage;
aggregator/partner applies own pricing.
notRated
Any other status is of internal interest of the Operator and should not be exchanged with the
Channel Partner. The following shows all statuses with comments on relevance:
Status
Meaning
Exchange Visibility
Comments
initialized
Usage record
created, validation
pending
❌
Internal
Not complete; not shared
rejected
Validation failed
❌
Internal
Excluded from exchange
validated
Format and
business rules
passed; ready for
rating
❌
Internal
Pre-rating only

© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 28
Status
Meaning
Exchange Visibility
Comments
corrected
Correction applied
to a previously
failed record
❌
Internal
May later progress to rated/notRated
rated
Successfully rated;
final price known
✅
External
(Marketplace
model)
Included in exchange when Operator
determines price
notRated
Validated but not
rated; price
determined by
partner
✅
External
(Wholesale model)
Included in exchange when pricing
handled externally
failed
Rating failed
❌
Internal
Operator-only
superseded
Usage replaced by
a newer record
❌
Internal
Do not exchange obsolete data
The filtering of eligible ProductUsage records by status is defined in the
ExportJob.query
parameter of the TMF937
/exportJob
operation. Example:
query: status=
notRated
,
rated
&completionDate.gte=2025-08-
10T00:00:00.000Z&completionDate.lt=2025-09-09T59:59:59.999Z
In TMF937, only those records with
status=rated
or
status=notRated
are included in
the exported file.

ProductUsageSpecification (not part of the OAS)
NOTE
For Open Gateway TMF937 MVP, it has been decided
•
to not require exposure of ProductUsageSpecification. The productUsage specification is
materialized by the strongly-typed schemas of ProductUsage using polymorphism.
•
all Operators have to use standard schemas available in
GSMA-Open-Gateway/Operate-
API-References:
Repository
to
store
schemas
and
information
from
the
TMF
Operate
APIs. To be read in conjunction with TMF Operate APIs
for Camara API usages. So that
it permits all Operators to use exactly same attribute names for the usage characteristics
of each Camara API.
•
the definitions of these schemas are done under Operate API stream within TM Forum in
collaboration with GSMA
•
each Operator can decide to extend the standard schemas with additional attributes if
needed, but the standard required ones must be included and not modified (same name
and same semantics) to ensure interoperability across Operators and Channel Partners.
Definition
A
ProductUsageSpecification
defines
the
reusable
structure,
semantics,
and
measurement
dimensions
of
a
ProductUsage
record.
It
acts
as
the
blueprint
for
how
a
specific
type
of
usage
event
(e.g.,
API
call,
session,
query)
is
captured,
identified,
and
interpreted for charging, analytics, and settlement purposes.
Open Gateway Product Usage User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 30
Each ProductUsageSpecification is:
•
Reusable
across multiple ProductOfferings, even when pricing or allowances differ.
•
Independent
of commercial terms (e.g., tiers, bundles, discounts).
•
Stable
across partners and markets, enabling interoperability and catalog modularity.
In
TMF937,
ProductUsageSpecification
defines
the
structure
of
the
exchanged
usage
records
,
ensuring
that
both
Operator
and
Channel
Partner
interpret
the
usage
data
consistently.
It
is
not
exchanged
dynamically
via
the
API
but
serves
as
a
reference
definition
to interpret ProductUsage attributes within each file.

NOTE
Usage type is a classification of usage based on the characteristics, used for
reporting, invoice grouping and more. Type of Event defines how a usage
event is valued. It reflects the physical or logical dimension that the product
uses

the
future we will cover also subscription and notification based APIs that may
have other requirements.

SUPPORT OF POLYMORPHISM AND
EXTENSION PATTERNS
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities,
for
instance
an
OpenGatewayExportJob inheriting properties from the ExportJob entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
a
list
of
ExportJob
instances
some
may
be
instances
of
OpenGatewayExportJob. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources
of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.
The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance a ExportJobRef
object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such
as
OpenGatewayExportJobRef,
and
not
the
class
type
of
the
referred
object.
However
since
reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended.

RESOURCE MODEL
The Product Usage Operate API works in the Product Usage domain of the TM Forum SID,
with ProductUsage and ProductUsageSpecification as the core entities and ExportJob as the
mechanism
to
package
and
deliver
usage
externally.
File-level
metadata
and
signatures
complement these to ensure integrity, traceability and secure delivery between Operator and
Channel Partner.
At
this
time
there
are
no
business
requirements
for
exposing
individual
ProductUsage
records via this API; the exposure of ProductUsage in an aggregated file is enough for now
and permits to be more efficient due to high volume. There are no business requirements for
exposing capability to request an exportJob (the POST exportJob operation is expected to
be performed by the Operator’s internal system).
Entity
Role
ExportJob
Asynchronous task that selects, packages and
exposes ProductUsage data as downloadable
files.
ExportJob
Definition
An
ExportJob
represents
an
asynchronous
task
that
generates
and
packages
finalized
ProductUsage
records
for
delivery
from
a
Serving
Party
(Operator)
to
a
Served
Party
(Channel Partner).
In
TMF937,
the
ProductUsage
Export
capability
builds
upon
the
TMF635
Product
Usage
Management API v5.0, which now includes the ExportJob resource as a native, embedded
capability, allowing creation, monitoring, and event publication to occur under a single API
endpoint (/exportJob).
TMF937 adopts this model and specializes it for inter-party exchange, adding file structure,
naming, metadata, and security rules specific to Operator–Channel Partner usage export.
Each ExportJob instance executes a single data extraction based on pre-agreed parameters
defined
in
the Agreement
mapped
into
the
selection
criteria
expressed
in
the
query
(time
window, status).
(can be planned for future version) When processing completes, an ExportJobCreateEvent
notifies the partner that data is available for download.

Semantic alignment.
Purpose in TMF937
In TMF937, the ExportJob is the entity allowing delivering a list of finalized ProductUsage
across
organizational
boundaries.
It
provides
asynchronous,
secure,
and
verifiable
data
exchange, supporting both Marketplace Aggregator and Wholesale models.
TMF937 exposes in a read-only mode pre-configured exportJobs. The creation and update
operations of the exportJob resource are not managed via this API.
An ExportJob:
•
Selects eligible ProductUsage records (status = rated or notRated).
•
Packages
them
according
to
agreed
parameters
(for
instance
first
productUsage
creationDate and last creationDate).
•
Generates
a
downloadable
ZIP
file
containing
usage
data,
metadata,
and
an
optional
signature.
•
Notifies the Channel Partner upon completion.
Managed Entity and Task Resource Models
OpenGatewayExportJob resource
The base class for an ExportJob in the GSMA Open Gateway context, which extends the
generic ExportJob class.
Resource model
Open Gateway Product Usage User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 39
Figure 1 - OpenGatewayExportJob
Field descriptions
OpenGatewayExportJob fields
completionDate
A DateTime. Date on which the job was completed. This attribute
exists only when status is Succeeded.
contentType
A String. The format of the export file. In Open Gateway context
it is always application/gzip. ENUMERATED with values:
* application/gzip
creationDate
A DateTime. Date on which the job was created.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
path
A String. JSON Pointer relative to the API root node that points
to the resource acting as the source for streaming content to the
export destination specified by the ExportJob. Set to
/productUsage in Open Gateway context for this API.
ENUMERATED with values:
* /productUsage
query
A String. Used to scope the exported data. Identical to GET filter
construct using the API node defined by path as base. In Open
Gateway context, contains the query parameters used to filter
ProductUsage records for export, in particular start and end
completionDate.
signature
A String. JWS (JSON Web Signature) signature of the exported
zip file. Used to verify the authenticity and integrity of the
exported data.
Open Gateway Product Usage User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 40
status
A String. Status of the export job. In this context can only be
Succeeded. There is no requirement to share non Succeeded
ExportJob. ENUMERATED with values:
* Succeeded
url
A Uri. URL of the file containing exported data.
@baseType
A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class.
@schemaLocation
A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that defines additional
attributes and relationships.
@type
A String. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-class
Extensible name.
